tests.description: Reference: WRF 4.8 em_quarter_ss idealized supercell (GNU real32 build, dx = 2 km, dt = 12 s, 40 layers, WSM6 only, no radiation/surface physics) dumped by the instrumented ctessum-claude/WRF fork (module_esm_dump with esm_dump_inner hooks inside mp_wsm6_run of the ctessum-claude/MMM-physics fork, commit 52cfbd7) and replayed through the real64 (kind_phys = real64) standalone kernels/wsm6_driver at the WRF step. The test is POINTWISE and step-free: the inputs are the evaluation state the kernel dumps immediately before its warm-rain block (t_rates, q_rates, qc_rates, qr_rates: the state after the sub-step's sedimentation, melting and freezing; den and p: kernel arguments; qsat_w, rh_w, xl: the start-of-sub-step saturation block, see saturation.esm), the expected values are the process rates the kernel dumps right after evaluating them (`<rate>_raw`: after each process's own time-step limiter, before the mass-conservation rescaling) and the intermediates rslope*, work1 (f_diff), work2 (f_vent), denfac and the mp_wsm6_init coefficients, all taken from the real64 replay. No small-dt replay is used because WSM6's increments are not rate x dt (FORTRAN_BUGS.md note N3). Real64 replay vs real32 in-model dump (compare_dump.py): 1.5e-7 (praut), 8e-7 (pracw), 7.5e-6 (prevp), 3-4e-7 (rslope*), 1.5e-6 (work1), 3.6e-7 (work2); the real32 driver reproduces the dump bit-for-bit. Residual mismatch between this component and the real64 kernel comes from the kernel's default-real literals and the real32 WRF constants it receives (bvtr = 0.800000011920929, avtr = 841.9000244, den0 = 1.27999997, cpv = 1846.4000244, rv = 461.6000061, .104, 9.8, .55, .78, .31, 1.496e-6, 8.794e-5, 1.414e3), which this component takes at their nominal values from lib/wrf_constants.esm and wsm6_parameters.esm (FORTRAN_BUGS.md note N2-style rounding); measured with zero tolerances over all four tests it is <= 4.1e-7 relative in the rates (praut; pracw 1.2e-7, prevp 2.1e-7), 1.9e-7 in the coefficients (qck1), 2e-7 of the column maximum in f_diff, 1e-7 in f_vent and <= 9e-8 in rslope*, denfac. Tolerances are set 5-10x above the measured residual: relative 1e-6 on the mp_wsm6_init coefficients and on every spot check, absolute Linf_error bounds on the whole columns at 1e-6 of each column's maximum. The unlimited rates praut, pracw, prevp are the physics and are spot-checked at layers where the kernel's limiter is provably inactive (there the dumped `<rate>_raw` equals the unlimited rate); the limited observeds praut_lim, pracw_lim, prevp_lim are compared with the dumped `<rate>_raw` over the whole column. Regime: supercell step 250 (t = 50 min), tile row j = 23, tile column i = 24 (the column with the strongest warm-rain rates): qc up to 2.4e-3, qr up to 1.3e-2 kg/kg, autoconversion active in layers 3-18 (qc > qc0), accretion and rain evaporation/condensation in layers 1-16 (rain present), rh_w 0.68-1.36 so prevp changes sign within the column, freezing level at layer 9. No limiter is active anywhere in the column (checked in the dump: no praut/pracw equals qc/dtcld and no prevp equals -qr/dtcld or satdt/2), so the whole `<rate>_raw` columns equal the unlimited rates.

The component's lev axis has 40 layers (the supercell size, esm-spec 6.6 tests cannot rebind a metaparameter), so this test uses the lowest 40 of the 59 SCM layers; the rates are pointwise, so the truncation is exact.
